source: Principal's instructions, pasted verbatim 2026-10-26 ('Claude instructions' and 'Legal instructions'). The text below is his; the citation map, held_out and state_overlay are Legal's reading of the shelved authority.
purpose: Pre-suit instrument that demands any private entity or agency produce the SSA-89 consent form or equivalent documentation for every SSN collection event tied to the user's identity. Not a lawsuit — a documented request that converts their silence or refusal into evidence.
build_requirements: One — a demand template that names the requester, states the SSA-89 requirement under the Consent Based SSN Verification program, cites fifteen U.S.C. sixteen eighty-one-b for FCRA permissible purpose, and fifteen U.S.C. sixteen eighty-one-s-two for the eCBSV five-year retention obligation where applicable.
Two — a tracking ledger that logs every demand sent: date, recipient, method, response received, response content, and whether the form was produced.
Three — an escalation flag that triggers when a recipient either refuses, ignores past thirty days, or produces a form whose stated purpose doesn't match their actual use.
Four — integration with the existing identity-theft affidavit workflow so any demand that returns a mismatch auto-generates a draft FCRA sixteen eighty-one-s complaint outline.

Five — state-by-state privacy law overlay: California, Texas, and Virginia have their own SSN protection statutes that may impose independent duties the federal form doesn't reach. Map those per recipient.
Six — output format should be a single markdown file per demand cycle with a summary table at top: recipient, form demanded, produced yes or no, mismatch flag, escalation status.

doctrine.text: Never cite SSA-521 as leverage — that form is for SSA's own verification requests, not third-party consent. The correct instrument is SSA-89 for private requesters and eCBSV consent retention for financial institutions.
The demand is a pre-suit instrument, not a cause of action. Its value is evidentiary — it creates a paper trail that either confirms compliance or documents willful avoidance.
When a recipient cannot produce the form, Legal's analysis should treat that absence as supporting a willful FCRA or Privacy Act theory, not as proof of a standalone violation.

Cross-reference every demand result against the continuing-violation theory on HUD-VASH annual renewals and the DoDI one thousand point thirty lifetime-restriction argument — the SSA form gap and the identifier-use gap are separate walls that can be pressed together in one filing.
Flag any recipient that is a federal agency operating under a routine-use exception — those have a different defense posture and need separate treatment.
Before any demand is sent to a financial institution, confirm whether eCBSV applies and whether the five-year retention window is still open.
This doctrine does not authorize contacting third parties on the user's behalf without explicit written authorization per demand cycle.

fcra_permissible_purpose.use: FCRA permissible purpose (requirement One, as instructed)

ecbsv_consent.quote: a permitted entity may submit a request to the database or similar resource described in subsection (c) only— (A) pursuant to the written, including electronic, consent received by a permitted entity from the individual who is the subject of the request; and (B) in connection with a credit transaction or any circumstance described in section 1681b of title 15

ecbsv_retention.quote: The entity will retain sufficient records to demonstrate its compliance with its certification and this section for a period of not less than 2 years.

privacy_act_routine_use.use: routine-use disclosure by a federal agency (doctrine rule 5)

fcra_willful.use: the willful theory doctrine rule 3 names

fcra_limitations.use: the clock a regulator complaint does not stop

held_out.instructed_for: the eCBSV five-year retention obligation (requirement One)
held_out.finding: Opened 2026-10-26: the shelved text (21,991 characters) contains no reference to eCBSV, consent, or record retention - it is the furnisher-duties section. eCBSV's retention clause is 42 U.S.C. 405b(e)(4), 'not less than 2 years', and no five-year period appears anywhere in 405b. A five-year figure may come from SSA's eCBSV user agreement, which is not on the shelf.
held_out.status: held for the principal - keep or drop; not placed in any demand until he says

five_year_window.basis: doctrine rule 6 and requirement One; no shelved text states five years
five_year_window.reported_beside: the statutory minimum in 42 U.S.C. 405b(e)(4), 2 years
